1	---
2	title: "Zener Language"
3	description: "Hardware Description Language for PCB design"
4	---
5	
6	# Specification
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	Zener is a domain-specific language built on top of
11	[Starlark](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md) for
12	describing PCB schematics. It provides primitives for defining components, symbols, nets,
13	interfaces, and modules in a type-safe, composable manner.
14	
15	This specification describes the language extensions and primitives added on top
16	of Starlark. For the base Starlark language features, please refer to the
17	[Starlark specification](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md) and the
18	[starlark-rust types extension](https://github.com/facebook/starlark-rust/blob/main/docs/types.md).
19	
20	## Table of Contents
21	
22	1. [Modules and Imports](#modules-and-imports)
23	2. [Nets and Interfaces](#nets-and-interfaces)
24	3. [Components and Symbols](#components-and-symbols)
25	4. [Modules](#modules)
26	5. [Utilities](#utilities)
27	6. [Schematic Position Comments](#schematic-position-comments)
28	
29	## Modules and Imports
30	
31	Each `.zen` file is a Starlark module that can be used in two ways:
32	
33	1. **Symbol imports** with `load()` bring functions and types into scope:
34	   ```python
35	   load("./utils.zen", "helper")
36	   load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Resistance")
37	   ```
38	
39	2. **Schematic modules** with `Module()` create instantiable subcircuits:
40	   ```python
41	   Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
42	   Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
43	   ```
44	
45	### Import Paths
46	
47	Import paths support local files, stdlib, and remote packages:
48	
49	```python
50	# Local file (relative to current file)
51	load("./utils.zen", "helper")
52	
53	# Stdlib (version controlled by toolchain)
54	load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Resistance")
55	load("@stdlib/interfaces.zen", "Spi")
56	
57	# Remote packages (version declared in pcb.toml)
58	Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
59	TPS54331 = Module("github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331/TPS54331.zen")
60	```
61	
62	The `@stdlib` alias is special and virtual—its content is controlled by the toolchain. You don't need to declare it in `[dependencies]`.
63	
64	Remote package URLs don't include version information. Versions are declared separately in `pcb.toml`, so import statements remain stable across upgrades:
65	
66	```toml
67	[dependencies]
68	"github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331" = "1.0"
69	```
70	
71	### Dependency Resolution
72	
73	Dependencies are automatically resolved when you import remote packages. The toolchain discovers dependencies from import paths, resolves versions, downloads packages, and updates `pcb.toml`.
74	
75	`@stdlib` is toolchain-managed and implicit.
76	
77	KiCad symbol/footprint/model linkage is configured by workspace-level `[[workspace.kicad_library]]` entries.
78	Dependencies are still declared in `[dependencies]`, and auto-deps can add them from imports.
79	
80	If `[[workspace.kicad_library]]` is omitted, the toolchain defaults the workspace to two entries:
81	- KiCad 9: `version = "9.0.3"` and `models.KICAD9_3DMODEL_DIR = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D"`
82	- KiCad 10: `version = "10.0.0"` and `models.KICAD10_3DMODEL_DIR = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D"`
83	
84	Both default entries use:
85	- `symbols = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-symbols"`
86	- `footprints = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints"`
87	- `parts = "https://kicad-mirror.api.diode.computer/kicad-parts-{version}.toml"`
88	- `http_mirror = "https://kicad-mirror.api.diode.computer/{repo_name}-{version}.tar.zst"`
89	
90	`parts` and `http_mirror` are optional and support template placeholders:
91	- `{repo}`
92	- `{repo_name}`
93	- `{version}`
94	- `{major}`
95	
96	Version resolution uses Minimal Version Selection (MVS), which selects the *minimum* version satisfying all constraints rather than the newest. This ensures deterministic builds—the same code always resolves to the same versions regardless of what exists upstream.
97	
98	The lockfile (`pcb.sum`) records exact versions and cryptographic hashes. Commit it to version control for reproducible builds across machines.
99	
100	See [Packages](/pages/packages) for complete details on version resolution and dependency commands.
101	
102	### Project Structure
103	
104	Zener projects use one of two repository shapes: a board repository or a registry repository.
105	
106	#### Board repository
107	
108	A board repository contains one board plus any local modules and components it owns. Create one with `pcb new board <name> <repo-url>`:
109	
110	```
111	MainBoard/
112	├── pcb.toml              # Workspace and board manifest
113	├── pcb.sum               # Dependency lock file
114	├── MainBoard.zen
115	├── modules/
116	│   └── PowerSupply/
117	│       ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
118	│       └── PowerSupply.zen
119	└── components/
120	    └── TPS54331/
121	        ├── pcb.toml
122	        └── TPS54331.zen
123	```
124	
125	Use `pcb new package <path>` to add modules or components inside the board repository.
126	
127	**Manifest** (root `pcb.toml`):
128	
129	```toml
130	[workspace]
131	repository = "github.com/myorg/MainBoard"
132	pcb-version = "0.3"
133	endpoint = "diode.computer"
134	
135	[board]
136	name = "MainBoard"
137	path = "MainBoard.zen"
138	description = "Replace with concise board description."
139	```
140	
141	- `name`: Optional Diode workspace name override for board release uploads. When omitted, publish uses the first path segment of `repository`, such as `myorg` from `github.com/myorg/MainBoard`.
142	- `repository`: Git remote URL (used to derive package URLs for publishing)
143	- `pcb-version`: Compatible `pcbc` toolchain release lane (e.g., `"0.3"`) or the explicit moving `"nightly"` channel. For semver lanes, `pcb` selects the newest installed toolchain in that lane, installing the newest available patch release for the lane when none is installed. It never auto-upgrades a workspace across lanes such as `"0.3"` to `"0.4"`; run `pcb migrate` to make breaking-version upgrades explicit. Required for workspaces.
144	- `endpoint`: Optional Diode host suffix used for workspace-scoped app/API URLs. `"diode.computer"` resolves to `app.diode.computer` and `api.diode.computer`.
145	- `[board]`: Defines the repository's buildable board with `name`, entry `path`, and a short `description`
146	
147	V1 workspaces are no longer supported. If you have an older project, run `pcb migrate` to upgrade manifests and import paths.
148	Only the workspace root `pcb.toml` should contain a `[workspace]` section.
149	Board dependencies are also declared in the root manifest's `[dependencies]` table.
150	
151	#### Registry repository
152	
153	A registry repository contains reusable packages but no board at the root. It uses top-level `components/` and `modules/` directories:
154	
155	```
156	registry/
157	├── pcb.toml              # Workspace manifest
158	├── pcb.sum               # Dependency lock file
159	├── components/
160	│   └── TPS54331/
161	│       ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
162	│       ├── TPS54331.zen
163	│       ├── TPS54331.kicad_sym
164	│       └── TPS54331.kicad_mod
165	└── modules/
166	    └── UsbCSink/
167	        ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
168	        └── UsbCSink.zen
169	```
170	
171	Registry manifests include `[workspace]` but do not include `[board]`:
172	
173	```toml
174	[workspace]
175	repository = "github.com/myorg/registry"
176	pcb-version = "0.3"
177	```
178	
179	**Package manifest** (e.g., `modules/PowerSupply/pcb.toml`):
180	
181	```toml
182	[dependencies]
183	"github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331" = "1.0"
184	
185	parts = [
186	  { mpn = "TPS54331DR", symbol = "TPS54331.kicad_sym", symbol_name = "TPS54331", manufacturer = "Texas Instruments", qualifications = ["Preferred"] },
187	]
188	```
189	
190	Packages (modules, components) don't have a `[board]` section—they're libraries meant to be instantiated by boards or other modules.
191	
192	- `[dependencies]`: Version constraints for packages imported by this package
193	- `parts`: Optional default sourcing metadata keyed by symbol file. Each entry provides `mpn`, `manufacturer`, optional `qualifications`, optional `datasheet`, a package-relative `.kicad_sym` `symbol` path, and optional `symbol_name` to target a specific symbol within a multi-symbol library file. If `symbol_name` is omitted, the referenced `.kicad_sym` file must contain exactly one symbol; otherwise resolution fails and `symbol_name` is required. `Component()` sourcing precedence is described below.
194	
195	See [Packages](/pages/packages) for the complete manifest reference.
196	
197	### Prelude
198	
199	These stdlib symbols are available in every user `.zen` file without `load()`:
200	
201	- `io`, `input`, `output` — from `@stdlib/io.zen`
202	- `Net`, `Power`, `Ground`, `NotConnected` — from `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`
203	- `Board` — from `@stdlib/board_config.zen`
204	- `Layout`, `Part` — from `@stdlib/properties.zen`
205	
206	Local definitions shadow prelude symbols. The prelude does not apply to stdlib modules themselves.
207	
208	## Nets and Interfaces
209	
210	### Nets
211	
212	A `Net` represents an electrical connection between component pins. `Net` is the base net type; specialized types like `Power`, `Ground`, and `NotConnected` add metadata (schematic symbols, voltage) while remaining fundamentally nets.
213	
214	```python
215	load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Impedance")
216	
217	# Basic nets
218	CLK = Net()
219	DATA = Net(impedance=Impedance(50))  # controlled impedance
220	VREF = Net()  # inferred from assignment
221	
222	# Power and ground (prelude — no load needed)
223	VCC = Power("VCC_3V3", voltage="3.3V")
224	GND = Ground()  # inferred from assignment; voltage defaults to 0V
225	
226	# Intentionally unconnected
227	nc = NotConnected()
228	```
229	
230	`Net(name, voltage=None, impedance=None)` — all parameters optional. `Power` and `Ground` additionally accept a `voltage` parameter. Additional net types (`Analog`, `Pwm`, `Gpio`) are available from `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`.
231	
232	If a net constructor omits `name`, the assigned variable name is used when available:
233	
234	```python
235	CLK = Net()       # equivalent to Net("CLK")
236	VDD = Power()     # equivalent to Power("VDD")
237	```
238	
239	If you do spell out the same name that assignment inference would choose, Zener raises a style advice because the explicit name is redundant.
240	
241	Explicit constructor names still win, and unassigned constructor calls keep the existing generated-name behavior:
242	
243	```python
244	alias = Net("CLK")  # name is "CLK", not "alias"
245	Net()               # uses an auto-generated name
246	```
247	
248	Typed net fields validate against their declared field type and use the same string coercions as module inputs, so `Power("VCC", voltage="3.3V")` is equivalent to `Power("VCC", voltage=Voltage("3.3V"))`.
249	
250	Net types follow automatic conversion rules across `io()` boundaries: `NotConnected` promotes to any type (universal donor), any specialized type demotes to `Net`, but `Net` cannot automatically promote to specialized types. For explicit casting, call the target constructor with an existing net: `Power(net, voltage=Voltage("3.3V"))` or `Net(power_net)`.
251	
252	### Interfaces
253	
254	Interfaces define reusable connection patterns — groups of related nets. Define custom interfaces with `interface()`:
255	
256	```python
257	MyBus = interface(
258	    clk = Net("CLK"),
259	    data = Net("DATA"),
260	    enable = field(bool, True),
261	)
262	
263	bus = MyBus("BUS1", enable=False)
264	debug_bus = MyBus()
265	```
266	
267	Interface fields can be net instances, interface instances (for hierarchical composition), or `field()` specs. When instantiated, the first positional argument is an optional name; named arguments override defaults.
268	
269	If an interface instance omits its explicit name, the assigned variable name becomes the root used for generated child nets:
270	
271	```python
272	PowerIf = interface(
273	    vcc = Net(),
274	    gnd = Net("GND"),
275	)
276	
277	power = PowerIf()
278	# generated child nets become power_vcc and power_GND
279	```
280	
281	Only values generated by the interface definition are renamed this way. Caller-provided nets or interface instances keep their existing names:
282	
283	```python
284	ext = Net("EXT")
285	power = PowerIf(vcc = ext)
286	# ext stays "EXT"
287	```
288	
289	The standard library provides common interfaces (`Spi`, `I2c`, `Uart`, `Usb2`, `DiffPair`, `Pcie`, `Jtag`, `Swd`, etc.) in `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`. Helper functions `UartPair(a, b)` and `UsartPair(a, b)` create cross-connected pairs for point-to-point links.
290	
291	## Components and Symbols
292	
293	### Component
294	
295	Components represent physical electronic parts with pins, a schematic symbol, and a PCB footprint.
296	
297	```python
298	Component(
299	    name = "U1",
300	    symbol = my_symbol,
301	    pins = {
302	        "VCC": vcc,
303	        "GND": gnd,
304	        "OUT": output_net,
305	    },
306	    prefix = "U",
307	    part = Part(mpn="LM358", manufacturer="TI"),
308	)
309	```
310	
311	**Constructor**: `Component(**kwargs)`
312	
313	| Parameter | Required | Description |
314	|-----------|----------|-------------|
315	| `name` | yes | Instance name |
316	| `symbol` | yes | Symbol object defining the schematic representation |
317	| `pins` | yes | Dict mapping pin names to nets; omit KiCad `no_connect` pins |
318	| `part` | no | `Part` object specifying manufacturer sourcing (preferred) |
319	| `prefix` | no | Reference designator prefix (default: `"U"`) |
320	| `manufacturer` | no | Manufacturer name (legacy — prefer `part`) |
321	| `mpn` | no | Manufacturer part number (legacy — prefer `part`) |
322	| `footprint` | no | PCB footprint path (default: inferred from symbol `Footprint` property) |
323	| `type` | no | Component type string |
324	| `properties` | no | Additional properties dict |
325	| `spice_model` | no | Explicit `SpiceModel`; default: inferred from symbol `Sim.*` properties when present |
326	| `dnp` | no | Do Not Populate flag |
327	| `skip_bom` | no | Exclude from BOM (default: inverse of symbol `in_bom` flag) |
328	| `datasheet` | no | Datasheet URL or path (default: `part.datasheet`, then this component value, then symbol `Datasheet` property; local component paths resolved relative to the `.zen` file, symbol-local paths resolved relative to the `.kicad_sym` file) |
329	
330	When KiCad symbol pin metadata is available:
331	
332	- omitted `no_connect` pins are auto-wired to `NotConnected()`
333	- explicit `no_connect` entries warn
334	- `power_in` and `power_out` pins warn if connected to plain `Net` instead of `Power` or `Ground`
335	- if `spice_model` is omitted and the symbol provides `Sim.Library`, `Sim.Name`, `Sim.Device=SUBCKT`, `Sim.Pins`, and optional `Sim.Params`, `Component()` derives the SPICE model from those symbol properties
336	
337	### Part
338	
339	`Part` specifies manufacturer sourcing for a component. It is a prelude symbol — available in all `.zen` files without `load()`.
340	
341	**Constructor**: `Part(mpn, manufacturer, qualifications=[], datasheet=None)`
342	
343	| Parameter | Required | Description |
344	|-----------|----------|-------------|
345	| `mpn` | yes | Manufacturer part number (non-empty string) |
346	| `manufacturer` | yes | Manufacturer name (non-empty string) |
347	| `qualifications` | no | List of qualification strings (e.g. `["AEC-Q200"]`) |
348	| `datasheet` | no | Datasheet URL or path for this manufacturer part |
349	
350	**Attributes**: `.mpn`, `.manufacturer`, `.qualifications`, `.datasheet`
351	
352	Use `Part` with the `part` parameter on `Component()` for primary sourcing, and in `properties["alternatives"]` for alternate parts:
353	
354	```python
355	Component(
356	    name = "R1",
357	    symbol = Symbol(library="@kicad-symbols/Device.kicad_sym", name="R"),
358	    pins = {"P1": vcc, "P2": gnd},
359	    part = Part(
360	        mpn = "RC0603FR-0710KL",
361	        manufacturer = "Yageo",
362	        qualifications = ["AEC-Q200"],
363	        datasheet = "https://www.yageo.com/upload/media/product/products/datasheet/rchip/RC_L_51_RoHS_L_6.pdf",
364	    ),
365	    properties = {
366	        "alternatives": [
367	            Part(mpn="ERJ-3EKF1001V", manufacturer="Panasonic"),
368	        ],
369	    },
370	)
371	```
372	
373	During `pcb build`, reference designators are automatically allocated per-prefix (e.g. `R1`, `R2`, `C1`).
374	
375	### Symbol
376	
377	A `Symbol` represents a schematic symbol loaded from a KiCad symbol library.
378	
379	```python
380	ic_symbol = Symbol(library="TCA9554DBR.kicad_sym")
381	connector = Symbol(library="@kicad-symbols/Connector_Generic.kicad_sym", name="Conn_01x14")
382	```
383	
384	**Constructor**: `Symbol(library, name=None)`
385	
386	- `library`: Path to a `.kicad_sym` file. Supports local paths, `@kicad-symbols/` alias, and package paths.
387	- `name`: Symbol name within the library. Required for multi-symbol libraries; omit for single-symbol files.
388	
389	### Physical Quantities
390	
391	Physical quantities represent electrical values with a nominal value, optional min/max bounds, and a unit. Unit-specific constructors are provided by `@stdlib/units.zen` (e.g. `Voltage`, `Current`, `Resistance`, `Capacitance`, `Inductance`, `Impedance`, `Frequency`, `Temperature`):
392	
393	```python
394	load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Current", "Resistance", "Capacitance")
395	
396	# Point values
397	supply = Voltage("3.3V")
398	resistor = Resistance("4k7")     # 4.7kΩ using resistor notation
399	cap = Capacitance("100nF")
400	
401	# Ranges
402	input_range = Voltage("1.1–3.6V")
403	explicit_nominal = Voltage("11–26V (12V)")
404	
405	# Keyword bounds
406	operating = Voltage(min=11, max=26)
407	
408	# Arithmetic with automatic unit tracking
409	power = Voltage("3.3V") * Current("0.5A")   # → 1.65W
410	r = Voltage("5V") / Current("100mA")        # → 50Ω
411	```
412	
413	See `@stdlib/units.zen` for the complete list of unit constructors.
414	
415	**Properties**: `.value` (alias for `.nominal`), `.nominal`, `.min`, `.max`, `.tolerance`, `.unit`
416	
417	**Methods**: `.with_tolerance(t)`, `.with_value(v)`, `.with_unit(u)`, `.abs()`, `.diff(other)`, `.within(other)`, `.matches(other)`
418	
419	**Operators**: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (with unit tracking), `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `==` (strict equality against another `PhysicalValue`), unary `-`
420	
421	Use `.matches(other)` when you want coercive comparisons against strings or scalars such as `Voltage("5V").matches("5V")`.
422	
423	**String formatting**: Point values → `"3.3V"`. Symmetric tolerances → `"10k 5%"`. Ranges → `"11–26V (16V nom.)"`.
424	
425	### Generic Components
426	
427	Prefer generic components over raw `Component()` where possible. Generics come with standard symbols, footprints, and automatic BOM matching to house parts.
428	
429	```python
430	Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
431	Capacitor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Capacitor.zen")
432	
433	Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", package="0603", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
434	Capacitor(name="C1", value="100nF", package="0402", voltage="16V", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
435	```
436	
437	See `@stdlib/generics/` for the full list of available generics and their accepted parameters.
438	
439	## Modules
440	
441	Modules are reusable subcircuits — `.zen` files that declare their electrical interface and configuration, then build a circuit from them. They are the primary mechanism for hierarchical design.
442	
443	### Module()
444	
445	`Module()` loads a `.zen` file and returns a callable that instantiates it as a subcircuit:
446	
447	```python
448	PowerSupply = Module("./modules/PowerSupply.zen")
449	TPS54331 = Module("github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331/TPS54331.zen")
450	```
451	
452	Instantiation takes a required `name` and passes remaining arguments as inputs to the module's `io()` and `config()` declarations:
453	
454	```python
455	PowerSupply(name="PSU1", VIN=vin, VOUT=vout, GND=gnd, output_voltage="3.3V")
456	```
457	
458	Additional instantiation parameters:
459	- `properties`: Dict of property overrides for the module instance.
460	- `dnp`: Bool — mark as Do Not Populate.
461	- `schematic`: `"collapse"` or `"embed"` — controls schematic rendering of the subcircuit.
462	
463	### io()
464	
465	Declare a net or interface input for a module. This defines the module's electrical interface — the nets that a parent must (or may) connect when instantiating it.
466	
467	`io`, `input`, and `output` are prelude symbols re-exported from `@stdlib/io.zen`. The low-level builtin is `builtin.io(...)`.
468	
469	**Signature:** `io(name, typ_or_template, checks=None, optional=False, help=None, direction=None)` or `io(typ_or_template, checks=None, optional=False, help=None, direction=None)`
470	
471	- `name`: Optional explicit input name (conventionally UPPERCASE). If omitted, `io()` must be assigned to a top-level variable and that variable name is used.
472	- `typ_or_template`: A net type (`Net`, `Power`, `Ground`, etc.), an interface factory (`Spi`, `Uart`, etc.), a net template value, or an interface template value.
473	- `checks`: Optional check function or list of checks applied to the resolved value.
474	- `optional`: If `True`, a generated net/interface is used when the parent doesn't provide one. Default `False`.
475	- `help`: Help text for documentation and signatures.
476	- `direction`: Optional signature metadata. Must be `"input"` or `"output"` when provided.
477	
478	```python
479	VCC = io(Power)
480	GND = io(Ground)
481	VDD_3V3 = io(Power(voltage="3.3V"))
482	SPI_BUS = io(Spi("SPI"), optional=True)
483	SPI = io(Spi, optional=True)
484	DATA = io(Net)
485	CS = io(Net)
486	VIN = io(Power, direction="input")
487	VOUT = io(Power, direction="output")
488	```
489	
490	When `typ_or_template` is a template value, `io()` derives all three of these from it:
491	
492	- the placeholder type
493	- the default/template metadata
494	- implicit checks that constrain any provided input
495	
496	For example, `io(Power(voltage="1.8V - 3.6V"))` requires any supplied `Power` net to stay within that voltage range.
497	
498	Use `direction` for genuinely one-way ports like signal or power flow. Shared rails such as `GND` should usually remain plain `io()` declarations.
499	
500	When the explicit `name` matches the assigned variable name, omitting it is the preferred style and emits no redundancy advice.
501	
502	`input(name, typ_or_template, ...)` and `output(name, typ_or_template, ...)` are equivalent to `io(...)` with `direction="input"` or `direction="output"` respectively, and they also support omitted explicit names when assigned to top-level variables.
503	
504	```python
505	VIN = input(Power)
506	VDD = input(Power(voltage="3.3V"))
507	VOUT = output(Power)
508	CS = input(Net)
509	```
510	
511	### config()
512	
513	Declare a typed configuration input for a module. This defines parameters that control the module's behavior — values (not nets) provided by the parent.
514	
515	**Signature:** `config(name, typ, checks=None, default=None, allowed=None, optional=None, help=None)` or `config(typ, checks=None, default=None, allowed=None, optional=None, help=None)`
516	
517	- `name`: Optional explicit input name (conventionally lowercase). If omitted, `config()` must be assigned to a top-level variable and that variable name is used.
518	- `typ`: Expected type — primitives (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`), `enum`, or physical quantity constructors. `record()` types are not supported as module `config()` inputs.
519	- `checks`: Optional check function or list of checks.
520	- `default`: Default value. When provided, `optional` defaults to `True`.
521	- `allowed`: Optional finite set of allowed values. Accepts a `list`, `tuple`, or `dict` (using only the keys). Supported for `str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `enum`, and physical quantity types.
522	- `optional`: Explicit override. When `True` with no default, returns `None`.
523	- `help`: Help text.
524	
525	```python
526	value = config(Resistance)
527	package = config(Package, default=Package("0603"))
528	voltage = config(Voltage, optional=True)
529	manufacturer = config(str, default="Acme")
530	output_voltage = config(
531	    "output_voltage",
532	    Voltage,
533	    allowed=["0.8V", "0.9V", "1.0V", "1.1V"],
534	    default="1.0V",
535	)
536	```
537	
538	Values passed by the parent are automatically converted to the declared type when possible. String inputs can coerce to primitives (`"true"` → `True`, `"42"` → `42`, `"3.3"` → `3.3`), physical quantities (`"10k"` → `Resistance("10k")`), and enum variants (`"0603"` → `Package("0603")`). This is why `Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", package="0603", ...)` works even though `value` expects `Resistance` and `package` expects `Package`. When `allowed` is present, both the allowed set and the provided value are normalized through that same coercion path before membership is checked, and physical values are surfaced using their canonical formatting.
539	
540	As with `io()`, repeating the assigned variable name as an explicit `config()` name is redundant and triggers a style advice.
541	
542	### Writing a Module
543	
544	A module is a `.zen` file that declares its interface with `io()` and `config()`, then uses those values to build its circuit:
545	
546	```python
547	# modules/LedIndicator.zen
548	Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
549	Led = Module("@stdlib/generics/Led.zen")
550	
551	# Configuration
552	color = config(str, default="red")
553	r_value = config(str, default="330ohms")
554	
555	# Electrical interface
556	VCC = io(Power)
557	GND = io(Ground)
558	
559	# Internal net
560	led_anode = Net("LED_ANODE")
561	
562	# Circuit
563	Resistor(name="R1", value=r_value, package="0603", P1=VCC, P2=led_anode)
564	Led(name="D1", color=color, package="0603", A=led_anode, K=GND)
565	
566	# Layout
567	Layout(name="LedIndicator", path="layout/LedIndicator")
568	```
569	
570	Instantiated by a parent board:
571	
572	```python
573	# MainBoard.zen
574	LedIndicator = Module("./modules/LedIndicator.zen")
575	
576	vcc = Power("VCC_3V3", voltage="3.3V")
577	gnd = Ground("GND")
578	
579	LedIndicator(name="LED1", VCC=vcc, GND=gnd, color="green")
580	LedIndicator(name="LED2", VCC=vcc, GND=gnd, color="red")
581	
582	Board(name="MainBoard", layers=4, layout_path="layout/MainBoard")
583	```
584	
585	## Utilities
586	
587	### Board and Layout
588	
589	`Board()` configures PCB manufacturing parameters — stackup, design rules, and layout path. It is a prelude symbol.
590	
591	```python
592	Board(name="my_board", layers=4, layout_path="layout/my_board")
593	```
594	
595	Key parameters: `name`, `layout_path`, `layers` (2/4/6/8/10), `config` (explicit `BoardConfig`), `outer_copper_weight` (`"1oz"` or `"2oz"`), `copper_finish` (default `"ENIG"`).
596	
597	When `layers` is provided, `Board()` selects an appropriate default stackup, netclasses, and design rules. An explicit `config` is merged on top. See `@stdlib/board_config.zen` for `BoardConfig`, `Stackup`, `DesignRules`, `NetClass`, and preset stackups.
598	
599	`Layout()` defines reusable layout blocks for modules. When writing a module, use `Layout(name, path)` to associate a PCB layout with the subcircuit. See `@stdlib/properties.zen`.
600	
601	**`Simulation(name, setup=None, modifiers=None, bom_profile=...)`** — Attach inline simulation setup and component modifiers to the current module.
602	
603	`Simulation()` uses the same BOM-profile hook as `Layout()`: by default it registers the standard house-part matcher, `modifiers` run before `bom_profile`, and `bom_profile=None` disables automatic house matching for simulation-only evals.
604	
605	### File and Path
606	
607	**`File(path)`** — Resolve a path relative to the current `.zen` file. Raises an error if it doesn't exist.
608	
609	```python
610	datasheet = File("TPS54331.pdf")
611	footprint = File("@kicad-footprints/Resistor_SMD.pretty/R_0603_1608Metric.kicad_mod")
612	```
613	
614	**`Path(path, allow_not_exist=False)`** — Like `File()` but supports package paths and optional non-existence.
615	
616	```python
617	layout_dir = Path("layout/my_board", allow_not_exist=True)
618	```
619	
620	### Assertions
621	
622	Three global functions for validation and diagnostics:
623	
624	- **`check(condition, message)`** — Assert a condition. Raises an error with `message` if `condition` is false.
625	- **`error(message)`** — Raise an error unconditionally.
626	- **`warn(message)`** — Emit a warning diagnostic.
627	
628	```python
629	check(voltage <= Voltage("3.6V"), "Voltage exceeds maximum rating")
630	warn("Using deprecated parameter")
631	```
632	
633	### Electrical Checks
634	
635	`@stdlib/checks.zen` provides reusable check functions for typed inputs. For example, `voltage_within(range)` validates that a net with voltage metadata, or a direct `Voltage` value, falls within a specified range:
636	
637	```python
638	load("@stdlib/checks.zen", "voltage_within")
639	vref = config(Voltage, checks=voltage_within("1.1–3.6V"))
640	```
641	
642	Template-first `io()` can also contribute implicit checks. A typed net template with a meaningful `voltage` property enforces the same containment rule automatically:
643	
644	```python
645	VCC = io(Power(voltage="1.1–3.6V"))
646	```
647	
648	Explicit `checks=` still run as well, after type validation and any template-derived implicit checks.
649	
650	### E-Series
651	
652	`@stdlib/utils.zen` provides functions to snap values to standard resistor/capacitor E-series: `e3()`, `e6()`, `e12()`, `e24()`, `e48()`, `e96()`, `e192()`.
653	
654	```python
655	load("@stdlib/utils.zen", "e96")
656	r = e96(Resistance("4.8k"))  # → 4.87kΩ (nearest E96 value)
657	```
658	
659	## Schematic Position Comments
660	
661	Zener supports persisted schematic placement metadata in trailing comment blocks.
662	These comments are consumed by tooling and surfaced in netlist output.
663	**Do not edit these comments directly.**
664	
665	Canonical line format:
666	
667	```text
668	# pcb:sch <id> x=<f64> y=<f64> rot=<f64> [mirror=<x|y>]
669	```
670	
671	- `id`: Position key (component or net symbol key in comment form, e.g. `R1`, `VCC.1`)
672	- `x`, `y`: Schematic coordinates
673	- `rot`: Rotation in degrees
674	- `mirror` (optional): Mirror axis (`x` or `y`)
675	
676	Examples:
677	
678	```text
679	# pcb:sch R1 x=100.0000 y=200.0000 rot=0
680	# pcb:sch U1 x=150.0000 y=200.0000 rot=90 mirror=x
681	```
682

---
title: "Zener Language"
description: "Hardware Description Language for PCB design"
---

# Specification

## Overview

Zener is a domain-specific language built on top of
[Starlark](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md) for
describing PCB schematics. It provides primitives for defining components, symbols, nets,
interfaces, and modules in a type-safe, composable manner.

This specification describes the language extensions and primitives added on top
of Starlark. For the base Starlark language features, please refer to the
[Starlark specification](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md) and the
[starlark-rust types extension](https://github.com/facebook/starlark-rust/blob/main/docs/types.md).

## Table of Contents

1. [Modules and Imports](#modules-and-imports)
2. [Nets and Interfaces](#nets-and-interfaces)
3. [Components and Symbols](#components-and-symbols)
4. [Modules](#modules)
5. [Utilities](#utilities)
6. [Schematic Position Comments](#schematic-position-comments)

## Modules and Imports

Each `.zen` file is a Starlark module that can be used in two ways:

1. **Symbol imports** with `load()` bring functions and types into scope:
   ```python
   load("./utils.zen", "helper")
   load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Resistance")
   ```

2. **Schematic modules** with `Module()` create instantiable subcircuits:
   ```python
   Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
   Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
   ```

### Import Paths

Import paths support local files, stdlib, and remote packages:

```python
# Local file (relative to current file)
load("./utils.zen", "helper")

# Stdlib (version controlled by toolchain)
load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Resistance")
load("@stdlib/interfaces.zen", "Spi")

# Remote packages (version declared in pcb.toml)
Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
TPS54331 = Module("github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331/TPS54331.zen")
```

The `@stdlib` alias is special and virtual—its content is controlled by the toolchain. You don't need to declare it in `[dependencies]`.

Remote package URLs don't include version information. Versions are declared separately in `pcb.toml`, so import statements remain stable across upgrades:

```toml
[dependencies]
"github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331" = "1.0"
```

### Dependency Resolution

Dependencies are automatically resolved when you import remote packages. The toolchain discovers dependencies from import paths, resolves versions, downloads packages, and updates `pcb.toml`.

`@stdlib` is toolchain-managed and implicit.

KiCad symbol/footprint/model linkage is configured by workspace-level `[[workspace.kicad_library]]` entries.
Dependencies are still declared in `[dependencies]`, and auto-deps can add them from imports.

If `[[workspace.kicad_library]]` is omitted, the toolchain defaults the workspace to two entries:
- KiCad 9: `version = "9.0.3"` and `models.KICAD9_3DMODEL_DIR = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D"`
- KiCad 10: `version = "10.0.0"` and `models.KICAD10_3DMODEL_DIR = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D"`

Both default entries use:
- `symbols = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-symbols"`
- `footprints = "gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints"`
- `parts = "https://kicad-mirror.api.diode.computer/kicad-parts-{version}.toml"`
- `http_mirror = "https://kicad-mirror.api.diode.computer/{repo_name}-{version}.tar.zst"`

`parts` and `http_mirror` are optional and support template placeholders:
- `{repo}`
- `{repo_name}`
- `{version}`
- `{major}`

Version resolution uses Minimal Version Selection (MVS), which selects the *minimum* version satisfying all constraints rather than the newest. This ensures deterministic builds—the same code always resolves to the same versions regardless of what exists upstream.

The lockfile (`pcb.sum`) records exact versions and cryptographic hashes. Commit it to version control for reproducible builds across machines.

See [Packages](/pages/packages) for complete details on version resolution and dependency commands.

### Project Structure

Zener projects use one of two repository shapes: a board repository or a registry repository.

#### Board repository

A board repository contains one board plus any local modules and components it owns. Create one with `pcb new board <name> <repo-url>`:

```
MainBoard/
├── pcb.toml              # Workspace and board manifest
├── pcb.sum               # Dependency lock file
├── MainBoard.zen
├── modules/
│   └── PowerSupply/
│       ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
│       └── PowerSupply.zen
└── components/
    └── TPS54331/
        ├── pcb.toml
        └── TPS54331.zen
```

Use `pcb new package <path>` to add modules or components inside the board repository.

**Manifest** (root `pcb.toml`):

```toml
[workspace]
repository = "github.com/myorg/MainBoard"
pcb-version = "0.3"
endpoint = "diode.computer"

[board]
name = "MainBoard"
path = "MainBoard.zen"
description = "Replace with concise board description."
```

- `name`: Optional Diode workspace name override for board release uploads. When omitted, publish uses the first path segment of `repository`, such as `myorg` from `github.com/myorg/MainBoard`.
- `repository`: Git remote URL (used to derive package URLs for publishing)
- `pcb-version`: Compatible `pcbc` toolchain release lane (e.g., `"0.3"`) or the explicit moving `"nightly"` channel. For semver lanes, `pcb` selects the newest installed toolchain in that lane, installing the newest available patch release for the lane when none is installed. It never auto-upgrades a workspace across lanes such as `"0.3"` to `"0.4"`; run `pcb migrate` to make breaking-version upgrades explicit. Required for workspaces.
- `endpoint`: Optional Diode host suffix used for workspace-scoped app/API URLs. `"diode.computer"` resolves to `app.diode.computer` and `api.diode.computer`.
- `[board]`: Defines the repository's buildable board with `name`, entry `path`, and a short `description`

V1 workspaces are no longer supported. If you have an older project, run `pcb migrate` to upgrade manifests and import paths.
Only the workspace root `pcb.toml` should contain a `[workspace]` section.
Board dependencies are also declared in the root manifest's `[dependencies]` table.

#### Registry repository

A registry repository contains reusable packages but no board at the root. It uses top-level `components/` and `modules/` directories:

```
registry/
├── pcb.toml              # Workspace manifest
├── pcb.sum               # Dependency lock file
├── components/
│   └── TPS54331/
│       ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
│       ├── TPS54331.zen
│       ├── TPS54331.kicad_sym
│       └── TPS54331.kicad_mod
└── modules/
    └── UsbCSink/
        ├── pcb.toml      # Package manifest
        └── UsbCSink.zen
```

Registry manifests include `[workspace]` but do not include `[board]`:

```toml
[workspace]
repository = "github.com/myorg/registry"
pcb-version = "0.3"
```

**Package manifest** (e.g., `modules/PowerSupply/pcb.toml`):

```toml
[dependencies]
"github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331" = "1.0"

parts = [
  { mpn = "TPS54331DR", symbol = "TPS54331.kicad_sym", symbol_name = "TPS54331", manufacturer = "Texas Instruments", qualifications = ["Preferred"] },
]
```

Packages (modules, components) don't have a `[board]` section—they're libraries meant to be instantiated by boards or other modules.

- `[dependencies]`: Version constraints for packages imported by this package
- `parts`: Optional default sourcing metadata keyed by symbol file. Each entry provides `mpn`, `manufacturer`, optional `qualifications`, optional `datasheet`, a package-relative `.kicad_sym` `symbol` path, and optional `symbol_name` to target a specific symbol within a multi-symbol library file. If `symbol_name` is omitted, the referenced `.kicad_sym` file must contain exactly one symbol; otherwise resolution fails and `symbol_name` is required. `Component()` sourcing precedence is described below.

See [Packages](/pages/packages) for the complete manifest reference.

### Prelude

These stdlib symbols are available in every user `.zen` file without `load()`:

- `io`, `input`, `output` — from `@stdlib/io.zen`
- `Net`, `Power`, `Ground`, `NotConnected` — from `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`
- `Board` — from `@stdlib/board_config.zen`
- `Layout`, `Part` — from `@stdlib/properties.zen`

Local definitions shadow prelude symbols. The prelude does not apply to stdlib modules themselves.

## Nets and Interfaces

### Nets

A `Net` represents an electrical connection between component pins. `Net` is the base net type; specialized types like `Power`, `Ground`, and `NotConnected` add metadata (schematic symbols, voltage) while remaining fundamentally nets.

```python
load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Impedance")

# Basic nets
CLK = Net()
DATA = Net(impedance=Impedance(50))  # controlled impedance
VREF = Net()  # inferred from assignment

# Power and ground (prelude — no load needed)
VCC = Power("VCC_3V3", voltage="3.3V")
GND = Ground()  # inferred from assignment; voltage defaults to 0V

# Intentionally unconnected
nc = NotConnected()
```

`Net(name, voltage=None, impedance=None)` — all parameters optional. `Power` and `Ground` additionally accept a `voltage` parameter. Additional net types (`Analog`, `Pwm`, `Gpio`) are available from `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`.

If a net constructor omits `name`, the assigned variable name is used when available:

```python
CLK = Net()       # equivalent to Net("CLK")
VDD = Power()     # equivalent to Power("VDD")
```

If you do spell out the same name that assignment inference would choose, Zener raises a style advice because the explicit name is redundant.

Explicit constructor names still win, and unassigned constructor calls keep the existing generated-name behavior:

```python
alias = Net("CLK")  # name is "CLK", not "alias"
Net()               # uses an auto-generated name
```

Typed net fields validate against their declared field type and use the same string coercions as module inputs, so `Power("VCC", voltage="3.3V")` is equivalent to `Power("VCC", voltage=Voltage("3.3V"))`.

Net types follow automatic conversion rules across `io()` boundaries: `NotConnected` promotes to any type (universal donor), any specialized type demotes to `Net`, but `Net` cannot automatically promote to specialized types. For explicit casting, call the target constructor with an existing net: `Power(net, voltage=Voltage("3.3V"))` or `Net(power_net)`.

### Interfaces

Interfaces define reusable connection patterns — groups of related nets. Define custom interfaces with `interface()`:

```python
MyBus = interface(
    clk = Net("CLK"),
    data = Net("DATA"),
    enable = field(bool, True),
)

bus = MyBus("BUS1", enable=False)
debug_bus = MyBus()
```

Interface fields can be net instances, interface instances (for hierarchical composition), or `field()` specs. When instantiated, the first positional argument is an optional name; named arguments override defaults.

If an interface instance omits its explicit name, the assigned variable name becomes the root used for generated child nets:

```python
PowerIf = interface(
    vcc = Net(),
    gnd = Net("GND"),
)

power = PowerIf()
# generated child nets become power_vcc and power_GND
```

Only values generated by the interface definition are renamed this way. Caller-provided nets or interface instances keep their existing names:

```python
ext = Net("EXT")
power = PowerIf(vcc = ext)
# ext stays "EXT"
```

The standard library provides common interfaces (`Spi`, `I2c`, `Uart`, `Usb2`, `DiffPair`, `Pcie`, `Jtag`, `Swd`, etc.) in `@stdlib/interfaces.zen`. Helper functions `UartPair(a, b)` and `UsartPair(a, b)` create cross-connected pairs for point-to-point links.

## Components and Symbols

### Component

Components represent physical electronic parts with pins, a schematic symbol, and a PCB footprint.

```python
Component(
    name = "U1",
    symbol = my_symbol,
    pins = {
        "VCC": vcc,
        "GND": gnd,
        "OUT": output_net,
    },
    prefix = "U",
    part = Part(mpn="LM358", manufacturer="TI"),
)
```

**Constructor**: `Component(**kwargs)`

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | yes | Instance name |
| `symbol` | yes | Symbol object defining the schematic representation |
| `pins` | yes | Dict mapping pin names to nets; omit KiCad `no_connect` pins |
| `part` | no | `Part` object specifying manufacturer sourcing (preferred) |
| `prefix` | no | Reference designator prefix (default: `"U"`) |
| `manufacturer` | no | Manufacturer name (legacy — prefer `part`) |
| `mpn` | no | Manufacturer part number (legacy — prefer `part`) |
| `footprint` | no | PCB footprint path (default: inferred from symbol `Footprint` property) |
| `type` | no | Component type string |
| `properties` | no | Additional properties dict |
| `spice_model` | no | Explicit `SpiceModel`; default: inferred from symbol `Sim.*` properties when present |
| `dnp` | no | Do Not Populate flag |
| `skip_bom` | no | Exclude from BOM (default: inverse of symbol `in_bom` flag) |
| `datasheet` | no | Datasheet URL or path (default: `part.datasheet`, then this component value, then symbol `Datasheet` property; local component paths resolved relative to the `.zen` file, symbol-local paths resolved relative to the `.kicad_sym` file) |

When KiCad symbol pin metadata is available:

- omitted `no_connect` pins are auto-wired to `NotConnected()`
- explicit `no_connect` entries warn
- `power_in` and `power_out` pins warn if connected to plain `Net` instead of `Power` or `Ground`
- if `spice_model` is omitted and the symbol provides `Sim.Library`, `Sim.Name`, `Sim.Device=SUBCKT`, `Sim.Pins`, and optional `Sim.Params`, `Component()` derives the SPICE model from those symbol properties

### Part

`Part` specifies manufacturer sourcing for a component. It is a prelude symbol — available in all `.zen` files without `load()`.

**Constructor**: `Part(mpn, manufacturer, qualifications=[], datasheet=None)`

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `mpn` | yes | Manufacturer part number (non-empty string) |
| `manufacturer` | yes | Manufacturer name (non-empty string) |
| `qualifications` | no | List of qualification strings (e.g. `["AEC-Q200"]`) |
| `datasheet` | no | Datasheet URL or path for this manufacturer part |

**Attributes**: `.mpn`, `.manufacturer`, `.qualifications`, `.datasheet`

Use `Part` with the `part` parameter on `Component()` for primary sourcing, and in `properties["alternatives"]` for alternate parts:

```python
Component(
    name = "R1",
    symbol = Symbol(library="@kicad-symbols/Device.kicad_sym", name="R"),
    pins = {"P1": vcc, "P2": gnd},
    part = Part(
        mpn = "RC0603FR-0710KL",
        manufacturer = "Yageo",
        qualifications = ["AEC-Q200"],
        datasheet = "https://www.yageo.com/upload/media/product/products/datasheet/rchip/RC_L_51_RoHS_L_6.pdf",
    ),
    properties = {
        "alternatives": [
            Part(mpn="ERJ-3EKF1001V", manufacturer="Panasonic"),
        ],
    },
)
```

During `pcb build`, reference designators are automatically allocated per-prefix (e.g. `R1`, `R2`, `C1`).

### Symbol

A `Symbol` represents a schematic symbol loaded from a KiCad symbol library.

```python
ic_symbol = Symbol(library="TCA9554DBR.kicad_sym")
connector = Symbol(library="@kicad-symbols/Connector_Generic.kicad_sym", name="Conn_01x14")
```

**Constructor**: `Symbol(library, name=None)`

- `library`: Path to a `.kicad_sym` file. Supports local paths, `@kicad-symbols/` alias, and package paths.
- `name`: Symbol name within the library. Required for multi-symbol libraries; omit for single-symbol files.

### Physical Quantities

Physical quantities represent electrical values with a nominal value, optional min/max bounds, and a unit. Unit-specific constructors are provided by `@stdlib/units.zen` (e.g. `Voltage`, `Current`, `Resistance`, `Capacitance`, `Inductance`, `Impedance`, `Frequency`, `Temperature`):

```python
load("@stdlib/units.zen", "Voltage", "Current", "Resistance", "Capacitance")

# Point values
supply = Voltage("3.3V")
resistor = Resistance("4k7")     # 4.7kΩ using resistor notation
cap = Capacitance("100nF")

# Ranges
input_range = Voltage("1.1–3.6V")
explicit_nominal = Voltage("11–26V (12V)")

# Keyword bounds
operating = Voltage(min=11, max=26)

# Arithmetic with automatic unit tracking
power = Voltage("3.3V") * Current("0.5A")   # → 1.65W
r = Voltage("5V") / Current("100mA")        # → 50Ω
```

See `@stdlib/units.zen` for the complete list of unit constructors.

**Properties**: `.value` (alias for `.nominal`), `.nominal`, `.min`, `.max`, `.tolerance`, `.unit`

**Methods**: `.with_tolerance(t)`, `.with_value(v)`, `.with_unit(u)`, `.abs()`, `.diff(other)`, `.within(other)`, `.matches(other)`

**Operators**: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (with unit tracking), `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `==` (strict equality against another `PhysicalValue`), unary `-`

Use `.matches(other)` when you want coercive comparisons against strings or scalars such as `Voltage("5V").matches("5V")`.

**String formatting**: Point values → `"3.3V"`. Symmetric tolerances → `"10k 5%"`. Ranges → `"11–26V (16V nom.)"`.

### Generic Components

Prefer generic components over raw `Component()` where possible. Generics come with standard symbols, footprints, and automatic BOM matching to house parts.

```python
Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
Capacitor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Capacitor.zen")

Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", package="0603", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
Capacitor(name="C1", value="100nF", package="0402", voltage="16V", P1=vcc, P2=gnd)
```

See `@stdlib/generics/` for the full list of available generics and their accepted parameters.

## Modules

Modules are reusable subcircuits — `.zen` files that declare their electrical interface and configuration, then build a circuit from them. They are the primary mechanism for hierarchical design.

### Module()

`Module()` loads a `.zen` file and returns a callable that instantiates it as a subcircuit:

```python
PowerSupply = Module("./modules/PowerSupply.zen")
TPS54331 = Module("github.com/diodeinc/registry/components/TPS54331/TPS54331.zen")
```

Instantiation takes a required `name` and passes remaining arguments as inputs to the module's `io()` and `config()` declarations:

```python
PowerSupply(name="PSU1", VIN=vin, VOUT=vout, GND=gnd, output_voltage="3.3V")
```

Additional instantiation parameters:
- `properties`: Dict of property overrides for the module instance.
- `dnp`: Bool — mark as Do Not Populate.
- `schematic`: `"collapse"` or `"embed"` — controls schematic rendering of the subcircuit.

### io()

Declare a net or interface input for a module. This defines the module's electrical interface — the nets that a parent must (or may) connect when instantiating it.

`io`, `input`, and `output` are prelude symbols re-exported from `@stdlib/io.zen`. The low-level builtin is `builtin.io(...)`.

**Signature:** `io(name, typ_or_template, checks=None, optional=False, help=None, direction=None)` or `io(typ_or_template, checks=None, optional=False, help=None, direction=None)`

- `name`: Optional explicit input name (conventionally UPPERCASE). If omitted, `io()` must be assigned to a top-level variable and that variable name is used.
- `typ_or_template`: A net type (`Net`, `Power`, `Ground`, etc.), an interface factory (`Spi`, `Uart`, etc.), a net template value, or an interface template value.
- `checks`: Optional check function or list of checks applied to the resolved value.
- `optional`: If `True`, a generated net/interface is used when the parent doesn't provide one. Default `False`.
- `help`: Help text for documentation and signatures.
- `direction`: Optional signature metadata. Must be `"input"` or `"output"` when provided.

```python
VCC = io(Power)
GND = io(Ground)
VDD_3V3 = io(Power(voltage="3.3V"))
SPI_BUS = io(Spi("SPI"), optional=True)
SPI = io(Spi, optional=True)
DATA = io(Net)
CS = io(Net)
VIN = io(Power, direction="input")
VOUT = io(Power, direction="output")
```

When `typ_or_template` is a template value, `io()` derives all three of these from it:

- the placeholder type
- the default/template metadata
- implicit checks that constrain any provided input

For example, `io(Power(voltage="1.8V - 3.6V"))` requires any supplied `Power` net to stay within that voltage range.

Use `direction` for genuinely one-way ports like signal or power flow. Shared rails such as `GND` should usually remain plain `io()` declarations.

When the explicit `name` matches the assigned variable name, omitting it is the preferred style and emits no redundancy advice.

`input(name, typ_or_template, ...)` and `output(name, typ_or_template, ...)` are equivalent to `io(...)` with `direction="input"` or `direction="output"` respectively, and they also support omitted explicit names when assigned to top-level variables.

```python
VIN = input(Power)
VDD = input(Power(voltage="3.3V"))
VOUT = output(Power)
CS = input(Net)
```

### config()

Declare a typed configuration input for a module. This defines parameters that control the module's behavior — values (not nets) provided by the parent.

**Signature:** `config(name, typ, checks=None, default=None, allowed=None, optional=None, help=None)` or `config(typ, checks=None, default=None, allowed=None, optional=None, help=None)`

- `name`: Optional explicit input name (conventionally lowercase). If omitted, `config()` must be assigned to a top-level variable and that variable name is used.
- `typ`: Expected type — primitives (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`), `enum`, or physical quantity constructors. `record()` types are not supported as module `config()` inputs.
- `checks`: Optional check function or list of checks.
- `default`: Default value. When provided, `optional` defaults to `True`.
- `allowed`: Optional finite set of allowed values. Accepts a `list`, `tuple`, or `dict` (using only the keys). Supported for `str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `enum`, and physical quantity types.
- `optional`: Explicit override. When `True` with no default, returns `None`.
- `help`: Help text.

```python
value = config(Resistance)
package = config(Package, default=Package("0603"))
voltage = config(Voltage, optional=True)
manufacturer = config(str, default="Acme")
output_voltage = config(
    "output_voltage",
    Voltage,
    allowed=["0.8V", "0.9V", "1.0V", "1.1V"],
    default="1.0V",
)
```

Values passed by the parent are automatically converted to the declared type when possible. String inputs can coerce to primitives (`"true"` → `True`, `"42"` → `42`, `"3.3"` → `3.3`), physical quantities (`"10k"` → `Resistance("10k")`), and enum variants (`"0603"` → `Package("0603")`). This is why `Resistor(name="R1", value="10k", package="0603", ...)` works even though `value` expects `Resistance` and `package` expects `Package`. When `allowed` is present, both the allowed set and the provided value are normalized through that same coercion path before membership is checked, and physical values are surfaced using their canonical formatting.

As with `io()`, repeating the assigned variable name as an explicit `config()` name is redundant and triggers a style advice.

### Writing a Module

A module is a `.zen` file that declares its interface with `io()` and `config()`, then uses those values to build its circuit:

```python
# modules/LedIndicator.zen
Resistor = Module("@stdlib/generics/Resistor.zen")
Led = Module("@stdlib/generics/Led.zen")

# Configuration
color = config(str, default="red")
r_value = config(str, default="330ohms")

# Electrical interface
VCC = io(Power)
GND = io(Ground)

# Internal net
led_anode = Net("LED_ANODE")

# Circuit
Resistor(name="R1", value=r_value, package="0603", P1=VCC, P2=led_anode)
Led(name="D1", color=color, package="0603", A=led_anode, K=GND)

# Layout
Layout(name="LedIndicator", path="layout/LedIndicator")
```

Instantiated by a parent board:

```python
# MainBoard.zen
LedIndicator = Module("./modules/LedIndicator.zen")

vcc = Power("VCC_3V3", voltage="3.3V")
gnd = Ground("GND")

LedIndicator(name="LED1", VCC=vcc, GND=gnd, color="green")
LedIndicator(name="LED2", VCC=vcc, GND=gnd, color="red")

Board(name="MainBoard", layers=4, layout_path="layout/MainBoard")
```

## Utilities

### Board and Layout

`Board()` configures PCB manufacturing parameters — stackup, design rules, and layout path. It is a prelude symbol.

```python
Board(name="my_board", layers=4, layout_path="layout/my_board")
```

Key parameters: `name`, `layout_path`, `layers` (2/4/6/8/10), `config` (explicit `BoardConfig`), `outer_copper_weight` (`"1oz"` or `"2oz"`), `copper_finish` (default `"ENIG"`).

When `layers` is provided, `Board()` selects an appropriate default stackup, netclasses, and design rules. An explicit `config` is merged on top. See `@stdlib/board_config.zen` for `BoardConfig`, `Stackup`, `DesignRules`, `NetClass`, and preset stackups.

`Layout()` defines reusable layout blocks for modules. When writing a module, use `Layout(name, path)` to associate a PCB layout with the subcircuit. See `@stdlib/properties.zen`.

**`Simulation(name, setup=None, modifiers=None, bom_profile=...)`** — Attach inline simulation setup and component modifiers to the current module.

`Simulation()` uses the same BOM-profile hook as `Layout()`: by default it registers the standard house-part matcher, `modifiers` run before `bom_profile`, and `bom_profile=None` disables automatic house matching for simulation-only evals.

### File and Path

**`File(path)`** — Resolve a path relative to the current `.zen` file. Raises an error if it doesn't exist.

```python
datasheet = File("TPS54331.pdf")
footprint = File("@kicad-footprints/Resistor_SMD.pretty/R_0603_1608Metric.kicad_mod")
```

**`Path(path, allow_not_exist=False)`** — Like `File()` but supports package paths and optional non-existence.

```python
layout_dir = Path("layout/my_board", allow_not_exist=True)
```

### Assertions

Three global functions for validation and diagnostics:

- **`check(condition, message)`** — Assert a condition. Raises an error with `message` if `condition` is false.
- **`error(message)`** — Raise an error unconditionally.
- **`warn(message)`** — Emit a warning diagnostic.

```python
check(voltage <= Voltage("3.6V"), "Voltage exceeds maximum rating")
warn("Using deprecated parameter")
```

### Electrical Checks

`@stdlib/checks.zen` provides reusable check functions for typed inputs. For example, `voltage_within(range)` validates that a net with voltage metadata, or a direct `Voltage` value, falls within a specified range:

```python
load("@stdlib/checks.zen", "voltage_within")
vref = config(Voltage, checks=voltage_within("1.1–3.6V"))
```

Template-first `io()` can also contribute implicit checks. A typed net template with a meaningful `voltage` property enforces the same containment rule automatically:

```python
VCC = io(Power(voltage="1.1–3.6V"))
```

Explicit `checks=` still run as well, after type validation and any template-derived implicit checks.

### E-Series

`@stdlib/utils.zen` provides functions to snap values to standard resistor/capacitor E-series: `e3()`, `e6()`, `e12()`, `e24()`, `e48()`, `e96()`, `e192()`.

```python
load("@stdlib/utils.zen", "e96")
r = e96(Resistance("4.8k"))  # → 4.87kΩ (nearest E96 value)
```

## Schematic Position Comments

Zener supports persisted schematic placement metadata in trailing comment blocks.
These comments are consumed by tooling and surfaced in netlist output.
**Do not edit these comments directly.**

Canonical line format:

```text
# pcb:sch <id> x=<f64> y=<f64> rot=<f64> [mirror=<x|y>]
```

- `id`: Position key (component or net symbol key in comment form, e.g. `R1`, `VCC.1`)
- `x`, `y`: Schematic coordinates
- `rot`: Rotation in degrees
- `mirror` (optional): Mirror axis (`x` or `y`)

Examples:

```text
# pcb:sch R1 x=100.0000 y=200.0000 rot=0
# pcb:sch U1 x=150.0000 y=200.0000 rot=90 mirror=x
```

155	def deep_merge(base, override):
156	    """Deep merge two records, with override values taking precedence.
157	
158	    For records: recursively merges fields
159	    For lists: override replaces base entirely
160	    For primitives: override value used if not None
161	    """
162	
163	    if override == None:
164	        return base
165	    if base == None:
166	        return override
167	
168	    # Handle list types - override replaces entirely
169	    if type(base) == "list":
170	        return override if type(override) == "list" else base
171	
172	    # Check if both are records by checking if they have getattr/type
173	    base_type = type(base)
174	    override_type = type(override)
175	
176	    # Only merge if both are record types (not primitive types)
177	    if base_type == "record" and override_type == "record":
178	        merged = {}
179	
180	        # Get all field names from both records
181	        base_fields = dir(base)
182	        override_fields = dir(override)
183	        all_fields = set(base_fields + override_fields)
184	
185	        for field in all_fields:
186	            if field.startswith("_"):  # Skip private fields
187	                continue
188	
189	            base_val = getattr(base, field, None) if field in base_fields else None
190	            override_val = getattr(override, field, None) if field in override_fields else None
191	
192	            if override_val != None:
193	                if base_val != None and type(base_val) != "list":
194	                    # Recursively merge if both exist and not lists
195	                    merged[field] = deep_merge(base_val, override_val)
196	                else:
197	                    # Use override value (including for lists)
198	                    merged[field] = override_val
199	            elif base_val != None:
200	                # Keep base value when override is None but base has a value
201	
202	                merged[field] = base_val
203	            else:
204	                # Both are None, keep None
205	                merged[field] = None
206	
207	        # Extract record type from string representation
208	        base_str = str(base)
209	        if base_str.startswith("record["):
210	            type_name = base_str.split("[")[1].split("]")[0]
211	            if type_name == "BoardConfig":
212	                return BoardConfig(**merged)
213	            elif type_name == "DesignRules":
214	                return DesignRules(**merged)
215	            elif type_name == "Constraints":
216	                return Constraints(**merged)
217	            elif type_name == "PredefinedSizes":
218	                return PredefinedSizes(**merged)
219	            elif type_name == "Copper":
220	                return Copper(**merged)
221	            elif type_name == "Holes":
222	                return Holes(**merged)
223	            elif type_name == "Uvias":
224	                return Uvias(**merged)
225	            elif type_name == "Silkscreen":
226	                return Silkscreen(**merged)
227	            elif type_name == "SolderMask":
228	                return SolderMask(**merged)
229	            elif type_name == "Zones":
230	                return Zones(**merged)
231	            elif type_name == "ViaDimension":
232	                return ViaDimension(**merged)
233	            elif type_name == "NetClass":
234	                return NetClass(**merged)
235	
236	            elif type_name == "Stackup":
237	                return Stackup(**merged)
238	            elif type_name == "Material":
239	                return Material(**merged)
240	            elif type_name == "CopperLayer":
241	                return CopperLayer(**merged)
242	            elif type_name == "DielectricLayer":
243	                return DielectricLayer(**merged)
244	            else:
245	                error("Unknown record type for merge: " + type_name)
246	        else:
247	            error("Unable to determine record type from: " + base_str)
248	
249	    # Not records, override wins
250	    return override

253	def merge_configs(*configs: BoardConfig) -> BoardConfig:
254	    """Merge multiple BoardConfig objects, with later configs taking precedence.
255	
256	    Args:
257	        *configs: Variable number of BoardConfig objects to merge
258	
259	    Returns:
260	        BoardConfig: Merged configuration with later configs overriding earlier ones
261	    """
262	    if not configs:
263	        return BoardConfig()
264	
265	    result = configs[0]
266	    for config in configs[1:]:
267	        result = deep_merge(result, config)
268	
269	    return result

272	def merge_predefined_sizes(
273	    base: PredefinedSizes,
274	    track_widths: list | None,
275	    via_dimensions: list | None,
276	) -> PredefinedSizes:
277	    """Merge and deduplicate predefined sizes.
278	
279	    Args:
280	        base: Base PredefinedSizes to start with
281	        track_widths: Additional track widths to append (optional)
282	        via_dimensions: Additional via dimensions to append (optional)
283	
284	    Returns:
285	        PredefinedSizes: Merged, deduplicated, and sorted sizes
286	    """
287	    final_track_widths = base.track_widths if base.track_widths else []
288	    final_via_dimensions = base.via_dimensions if base.via_dimensions else []
289	
290	    if track_widths:
291	        final_track_widths = final_track_widths + track_widths
292	    if via_dimensions:
293	        final_via_dimensions = final_via_dimensions + via_dimensions
294	
295	    # Deduplicate and sort track_widths
296	    final_track_widths = sorted(list(set(final_track_widths)))
297	
298	    # Deduplicate and sort via_dimensions (by diameter, then drill)
299	    seen = {}
300	    deduped_vias = []
301	    for via in final_via_dimensions:
302	        key = str(via.diameter) + "_" + str(via.drill)
303	        if key not in seen:
304	            seen[key] = True
305	            deduped_vias.append(via)
306	    final_via_dimensions = sorted(deduped_vias, key=lambda v: (v.diameter, v.drill))
307	
308	    return PredefinedSizes(
309	        track_widths=final_track_widths,
310	        via_dimensions=final_via_dimensions,
311	    )

407	    """Define a PCB board with an optional board configuration.

409	    Args:
410	        name: Board configuration name
411	        layout_path: Path to the board layout file (e.g., PCB file)
412	        config: Optional BoardConfig overrides to merge with a layers-derived default.
413	                If layers is not provided, this is used directly.
414	        layers: Number of PCB layers (2, 4, 6, 8, or 10). Optional helper for deriving a default BoardConfig.
415	        outer_copper_weight: Outer copper weight ("1oz" or "2oz"). Default is "1oz".
416	                            Currently only 4-layer boards support 2oz outer copper.
417	        track_widths: Additional track widths (in mm) to append to the base configuration.
418	                     Values are deduplicated and sorted automatically.
419	        via_dimensions: Additional via dimensions to append to the base configuration.
420	                       Values are deduplicated and sorted automatically.
421	        layout_hints: Optional list of layout hints for the board
422	        default: Whether this is the default board configuration
423	
424	    Raises:
425	        error: If layers is provided but no default board configuration exists for
426	               the given layers and outer_copper_weight, and no explicit config is provided
427	        error: If outer_copper_weight is not "1oz" or "2oz"
428	        error: If 2oz copper is requested for unsupported layer counts (2L, 6L, 8L)
429	
430	    Behavior:
431	        - If layers is provided, selects appropriate stackup, netclasses, constraints,
432	          and predefined sizes based on layers and outer_copper_weight
433	        - If both layers and config are provided, config overrides are merged onto
434	          the layers-derived defaults
435	        - If neither config nor layers is provided, the board is still created without
436	          registering a board configuration
437	        - Custom track_widths and via_dimensions are appended to base configuration
438	        - All lists are deduplicated and sorted before use
439	    """

441	    # Validate input units
442	    if isinstance(outer_copper_weight, str):
443	        outer_copper_weight = CopperWeight(outer_copper_weight)
444	
445	    if isinstance(copper_finish, str):

# Enum Types
CopperWeight = enum("0.5oz", "1oz", "2oz")
CopperFinish = enum("HASL", "HASL Lead-free", "ENIG", "HAL SnPb", "HAL lead-free")

# Copper constraints - all clearances and widths for copper features
Copper = record(
    minimum_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum clearance between copper features
    minimum_track_width=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum track width
    minimum_connection_width=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum connection width (KiCad: m_MinConn)
    minimum_annular_width=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum annular ring width for vias
    minimum_via_diameter=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum via diameter
    copper_to_hole_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Clearance from copper to holes
    copper_to_edge_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Clearance from copper to board edge
)

# Hole constraints - drill sizes and clearances
Holes = record(
    minimum_through_hole=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum through hole diameter
    hole_to_hole_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum clearance between holes
)

# Micro via constraints - specialized via rules
Uvias = record(
    minimum_uvia_diameter=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum micro via diameter
    minimum_uvia_hole=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum micro via hole diameter
)

# Silkscreen constraints - text and graphics rules
Silkscreen = record(
    minimum_item_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum clearance for silkscreen items
    minimum_text_height=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum text height
    # Note: minimum_text_thickness is complex in KiCad API, not supported yet
)

# Solder mask constraints
SolderMask = record(
    clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Mask expansion / clearance from pads to mask opening
    minimum_width=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum mask web width
    to_copper_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Minimum solder-mask to copper-feature clearance
)

# Zone defaults constraints
Zones = record(
    minimum_clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Default zone-to-copper clearance
)

# All design rule constraints grouped together
Constraints = record(
    copper=field(Copper | None, None),
    holes=field(Holes | None, None),
    uvias=field(Uvias | None, None),
    silkscreen=field(Silkscreen | None, None),
    solder_mask=field(SolderMask | None, None),
    zones=field(Zones | None, None),
)

# Via dimensions for pre-defined sizes
ViaDimension = record(
    diameter=field(float | None, None),  # Via diameter in mm
    drill=field(float | None, None),  # Via drill size in mm
)

# NOTE: Differential pair dimensions are not supported due to missing SWIG template
# in KiCad Python API. The following would be needed in board.i:
# %template(DIFF_PAIR_DIMENSION_Vector) std::vector<DIFF_PAIR_DIMENSION>;

#     gap=float,                        # Gap between tracks in mm

    clearance=field(float | None, None),  # Clearance in mm
    track_width=field(float | None, None),  # Track width in mm
    via_diameter=field(float | None, None),  # Via diameter in mm
    via_drill=field(float | None, None),  # Via drill/hole in mm
    microvia_diameter=field(float | None, None),  # Microvia diameter in mm
    microvia_drill=field(float | None, None),  # Microvia drill/hole in mm
    diff_pair_width=field(float | None, None),  # Differential pair width in mm
    diff_pair_gap=field(float | None, None),  # Differential pair gap in mm
    diff_pair_via_gap=field(float | None, None),  # Differential pair via gap in mm
